prompt: High-resolution but optically degraded egocentric frame from a wrist-mounted fisheye industrial camera on a six-axis robotic arm in a fulfilment warehouse. The arm's parallel-jaw gripper clamps a single brown cardboard mailer on a black conveyor belt at the frame's centre. Severe barrel distortion bows the conveyor rails and the warehouse racking into curved lines at every edge. The image is grainy with fixed-pattern noise visible in the darker regions under the shelving, and the overhead LED bay lights bloom into blown-out oval smears at the top of the frame. The arm's own grey forearm housing and bundled cable loom are sharply visible entering from the upper-left, slightly out of the fisheye's focal sweet spot so the cable jacket text is smeared. A faded yellow floor-safety line warps into a parabola at the bottom edge, and a forklift's orange beacon is a streaky bokeh dot in the far background. The sensor timestamp reads 2024-11-14 03:47:12 in a fixed monospace font burned into the lower-left pixel row.

Egocentric fisheye capture from a wrist camera on a palletising robot, looking along the arm's extended reach as its vacuum-pad gripper lowers a single shrink-wrapped case of bottled water onto a half-stacked pallet. The fisheye pulls the pallet's wooden slats into a concave dish shape, and the shrink wrap's specular highlights clip to pure white in a hard band across the plastic. The arm's orange KUKA housing fills the left third of the frame, the paint chipped at the elbow joint revealing grey primer. Dust on the lens creates a soft haze ring around the blown-out ceiling lights, and a single dead pixel sits as a bright green dot at coordinates roughly upper-right. The warehouse concrete is oil-stained and cracked, and a hand-written paper sign taped to a post reads something illegible, warped beyond recognition by the lens distortion. ISO noise grain is uniform and fine, consistent with a 1/2-inch CMOS sensor at high gain.

High-resolution egocentric fisheye frame from a wrist-mounted camera on a robotic arm installing a single headlamp unit into a car body on an assembly line. The headlamp's chrome reflector and clear lens are at the centre, the arm's insertion tool pressing the unit into the body panel's socket. The fisheye distortion stretches the car's unpainted steel body into a curved wall at the edges, and the overhead gantry and cable trays arch like a tunnel. The image has a yellow-green colour cast from the mixed sodium-vapour and LED lighting, and the camera's auto-gain has pushed the shadows hard, revealing noisy purple-tinged banding in the dark cavity behind the headlamp. The arm's wrist encoder ring and a dangling zip-tied cable tag are in focus at the frame's top. Welding spatter marks on the body panel catch the light as tiny bright dots.

Egocentric fisheye still from a wrist camera on a seam-sealing robot in an automotive paint shop, looking at the arm's nozzle tip laying a bead of grey sealant along a single door-frame joint. The sealant rope is in sharp focus at the centre, wet and glossy, and the nozzle's stainless tip and the arm's white clean-room sleeve are visible above. The fisheye warps the spray booth's white walls into a curved enclosure, and the filtered ceiling panels bow upward. A fine mist of overspray from an adjacent booth drifts across the upper frame, and the lens has a permanent smear of dried sealant residue in the lower-right quadrant, creating a soft translucent blur over the booth floor. The image's colour response is flat and slightly magenta-shifted, and horizontal fixed-pattern noise bands are faintly visible across the mid-tones.

High-resolution egocentric fisheye frame from a wrist camera on a food-processing robotic arm, looking at its suction cup lifting a single vacuum-sealed salmon fillet from a stainless-steel drain tray. The fillet's pink flesh and the vacuum bag's wrinkled plastic are at the centre, and the suction cup's white silicone lip compresses the bag's surface. The fisheye bows the tray's raised edges and the conveyor's guide rails into U-shapes. Water droplets from a rinse cycle bead on the lens surface, creating out-of-focus bright circles over the upper portion. The stainless environment reflects the ceiling strip lights as long warped streaks, and the image has a cool blue-white colour temperature with no warmth. The arm's white food-safe housing and a stainless hose clamp are at the top of the frame, and a sanitation log clipboard hangs on the tiled wall, text unreadable at the fisheye periphery.

Egocentric fisheye capture from a wrist camera on a delta-style pick-and-place arm in a biscuit packaging line, looking down at its vacuum nozzle placing a single round shortbread biscuit into a plastic tray cavity. The biscuit's crumbly surface and embossed pattern are at the centre, and the nozzle's rubber tip is just releasing contact. The fisheye compresses the conveyor line into a narrow curved band, and the repeating pattern of tray cavities—most already filled—radiates outward in distorted rows. Flour dust coats the lens edges in a faint milky veil, and the fluorescent tube directly overhead is a hard blown-out stripe reflected in the plastic trays. Crumb debris is scattered on the belt surface, and a small clump of dough is stuck to the arm's pneumatic fitting. The sensor noise is low in the bright centre but spikes in the shadowed tray cavities with visible chroma noise in blue and red channels.

High-resolution egocentric fisheye frame from a wrist-mounted camera on a cobot in a PCB test cell, looking at its pogo-pin test fixture pressing down on a single populated circuit board. The fixture's spring-loaded gold pins make contact with the board's test pads at the centre, and the PCB's green solder mask, tiny SMD components, and silkscreen text are in macro detail. The fisheye distorts the test bench's edges and the cable harnesses into sweeping curves. The image has the characteristic flat, shadowless look of a ring-light illuminated scene, with slight specular glare off the solder joints. The arm's light-grey housing and a QR-code asset tag on the wrist joint are at the frame's top. An oscilloscope screen in the background displays a waveform, warped by the fisheye into a curved rectangle. Fixed-pattern column noise is faintly visible as vertical striping in the board's dark ground-plane areas.

Egocentric fisheye still from a wrist camera on a robotic arm in a cable-harness assembly station, looking at its pneumatic crimping tool squeezing a single metal terminal onto a stripped wire end. The terminal's brass body and the wire's copper strands are at the centre, clamped in the tool's steel jaws. The fisheye warps the workbench's peg board of hanging tools and the wire spools on the wall into a curved panorama. The image is sharp at the centre but shows significant lateral chromatic aberration at the edges—red and cyan fringing on the tool rack's metal edges. The lighting is a single adjustable-arm LED lamp creating a hard shadow from the crimping tool across the bench surface, and the arm's cable harness and a pneumatic quick-disconnect fitting are in the upper frame.

High-resolution egocentric fisheye frame from a wrist camera on a robotic arm in a steel-coil slitting facility, looking at its electromagnetic gripper engaging the edge of a single coiled steel strip on a decoiler mandrel. The steel's sheared edge is bright and sharp at the centre, and the magnet plate's flat face hovers millimetres above the coil surface. The fisheye dramatically warps the decoiler's massive drum and the overhead crane rails into sweeping arcs. The image has heavy industrial grime—oil mist hazes the mid-ground, and a film of ferrous dust on the lens creates a brownish vignette. The arm's heavy-duty yellow housing shows welding repair patches, and the factory floor's steel-plate decking and drainage channels are visible at the bottom edge, warped into a trough. The dynamic range is crushed—the bright steel edge clips white while the far corners are nearly black.

Egocentric fisheye capture from a wrist camera on a robotic arm in a concrete-pipe manufacturing plant, looking at its hydraulic clamp gripper rotating a single freshly cast concrete pipe segment on a curing rack. The pipe's rough grey surface and the mould seam line are at the centre, and the clamp's two padded jaws grip the pipe's circumference from opposite sides. The fisheye curves the curing rack's steel frame and the rows of other pipe segments into a receding tunnel shape. Steam from the curing process fogs the lower half of the image, and condensation droplets on the lens catch the overhead mercury-vapour lights as bright hexagonal flares. The arm's yellow housing is spattered with concrete slurry, and the image has the brownish-orange colour cast of mercury-vapour lighting with poor colour rendition. Sensor noise is aggressive in the steam-obscured regions.

High-resolution egocentric fisheye frame from a wrist-mounted camera on a cleanroom robotic arm, looking at its custom fork tool sliding a single glass petri dish from a stack in an incubator shelf. The dish's agar surface and a colony of bacterial growth are at the centre, visible through the glass lid. The fisheye distorts the incubator's interior shelves into curved lines, and the stainless-steel walls reflect the arm's white housing and the camera's own lens as a tiny circular highlight. The image is sterile and evenly lit by the incubator's internal LED, but the transition to the darker lab outside the incubator door creates a harsh exposure gradient—the lab side is underexposed with heavy luminance noise. The arm's HEPA-filtered joint covers and a barcode label on the wrist are in the upper frame. A digital temperature readout on the incubator wall reads 37.0°C, warped by the fisheye.

Egocentric fisheye still from a wrist camera on a robotic arm in a pharmaceutical blister-packing line, looking at its pick-and-place nozzle dropping a single white tablet into an aluminium blister cavity. The tablet is mid-fall between the nozzle tip and the cavity, caught as a slightly motion-blurred white disc. The blister sheet's grid of formed cavities radiates outward in fisheye distortion, most cavities already filled. The arm's stainless housing and a coiled air line are at the top of the frame. The lighting is intense overhead fluorescent creating hard reflections on the aluminium foil, and the camera's auto-exposure has darkened the overall image to compensate, pushing the arm's housing and the conveyor's side rails into noisy shadow. A batch-number sticker on the machine guard is partially readable at the warped left edge.

High-resolution egocentric fisheye frame from a wrist camera on a parcel-sorting robotic arm at a postal hub, looking at its belt-driven gripper clamping a single padded envelope on a high-speed tilt-tray sorter. The envelope's handwritten address and postage stamps are at the centre, and the gripper's two rubber belts pinch the envelope's edges. The fisheye warps the sorter's circular track of tilting trays into a curved river of parcels, most trays occupied. The image has significant motion blur on the trays moving in the background while the clamped envelope is frozen sharp—a rolling-shutter artefact creating a slight skew on the moving elements. The arm's grey housing and a reflective safety-vest strip on the cable loom are at the frame's top. The facility's high ceiling and dangling chain-link parcel chutes are dark and noisy at the periphery.

Egocentric fisheye capture from a wrist camera on a robotic arm in a recycling material recovery facility, looking at its claw-style gripper picking a single crushed aluminium can from a mixed-waste conveyor belt. The can's dented body and torn label are at the centre, gripped in the claw's three steel fingers. The fisheye distorts the conveyor's chaotic surface of mixed plastics, paper, and metal into a warped landscape of refuse. The image is dirty—a smear of unidentifiable residue coats the lens's lower edge, and moisture from the facility's misting system creates a diffuse haze. The lighting is uneven high-bay with one fixture visibly flickering, creating banding artefacts in the upper portion. The arm's housing is scratched and one joint cover is missing, exposing cabling. The concrete floor below the belt is wet and stained.

High-resolution egocentric fisheye frame from a wrist-mounted camera on a greenhouse harvesting arm, looking at its soft-finger gripper closing around a single cluster of cherry tomatoes on the vine. The tomatoes' glossy red skins and the vine's green stem are at the centre, and the gripper's three silicone-padded fingers approach from different angles. The fisheye warps the greenhouse's polycarbonate roof panels and drip-irrigation lines into a dome shape overhead. The camera's white balance is overwhelmed by the supplemental grow lights, giving the foliage an unnatural magenta-pink tint while the tomatoes appear oversaturated orange-red. Condensation from the humid environment fogs the lens in a gradient from the warmer edges inward, and water droplets on the tomato skins create bright specular highlights that clip to white. The arm's cable harness shows a repair splice wrapped in electrical tape.

Egocentric fisheye still from a wrist camera on a robotic pruning arm in a commercial vineyard, looking at its pneumatic secateurs positioned around a single grapevine cane. The cane's woody bark and a tendril are at the centre, bracketed by the secateurs' open curved blades. The fisheye warps the vineyard row into a green tunnel of leaf canopy and wire trellis. Bright afternoon sunlight creates extreme dynamic range—the sky visible through leaf gaps is pure white, while the shaded cane is underexposed with heavy shadow noise. Pollen and dust suspended in the air scatter the backlight into visible rays across the upper frame. The arm's housing is mud-splashed from ground-level operation, and a spider has built a small web between the camera housing and the arm's wrist joint, visible as a few out-of-focus silk strands across the upper-right corner.

High-resolution egocentric fisheye frame from a wrist camera on a fabric-handling robot in a garment cutting room, looking at its needle-array gripper pressing into a single ply of black jersey knit on a vacuum cutting table. The fabric's stretch-knit texture and the gripper's rows of thin steel needles penetrating the surface are at the centre. The fisheye warps the cutting table's large flat surface and the overhead projector's alignment laser grid into curving lines. The black fabric absorbs light, causing the camera's auto-gain to crank up, introducing heavy luminance noise across the dark material while the white cutting-table border and the arm's housing are overexposed. A piece of tailor's chalk and a pattern weight are at the warped table edge, and lint fibres floating in the air catch the overhead light as tiny bright streaks.

Egocentric fisheye capture from a wrist camera on a robotic arm in a furniture factory, looking at its vacuum-cup gripper lifting a single unfinished oak drawer front from a sanding station conveyor. The wood's open grain and sanding scratches are in high-resolution detail at the centre, and the vacuum cup's black rubber lip leaves a faint circular compression mark on the raw surface. The fisheye distorts the sanding station's dust-collection hood and the conveyor's rubber belt into sweeping curves. Fine sawdust hangs in the air, softening the background into a warm haze, and a coating of dust on the camera lens reduces contrast across the entire image. The arm's housing shows a layer of pale wood dust in every crevice, and the factory's extraction ducting and hanging power cables curve overhead. The colour is a uniform warm amber from the sawdust haze and the overhead sodium lights.

High-resolution egocentric fisheye frame from a wrist camera on a robotic arm on a craft-brewery canning line, looking at its foam-padded gripper rotating a single aluminium beer can under a label applicator. The can's freshly applied label—still slightly misaligned—and the bare aluminium above the label edge are at the centre. The gripper's two semicircular pads grip the can's body, and the applicator's rubber roller is visible pressing the label's trailing edge. The fisheye warps the canning line's stainless manifolds and CO2 hoses into curved shapes, and a puddle of spilled beer on the stainless tabletop reflects the overhead lights in a warped bright patch. The image has a slight amber tint from the beer residue misting onto the lens, and condensation from the cold cans creates a fog gradient at the bottom of the frame. The arm's cable harness is damp and a zip tie has come loose, dangling.

Egocentric fisheye still from a wrist camera on a robotic arm in a tyre-inspection cell, looking at its roller-probe end effector pressing against the inner sidewall of a single inflated tyre mounted on a spin fixture. The tyre's interior rubber surface and the steel belt cords faintly visible beneath are at the centre, and the probe's steel roller indents the sidewall under spring pressure. The fisheye warps the tyre's circular form into a near-sphere filling the frame, and the spin fixture's chuck and drive motor are visible through the tyre's centre bore. The lighting is a UV-spectrum inspection lamp, giving the rubber an unnatural blueish fluorescence and making a small internal defect—a trapped air bubble—glow as a bright spot. The arm's housing is black rubber-coated for the inspection environment, and the camera's UV response creates purple fringing on every high-contrast edge. The overall image feels clinical and alien in its colour palette—deep violet shadows, fluorescent blue highlights, and no natural tones.
